questions.prompt: Compare po, p, and v in LLDB. Explain when you would use each command and the trade-offs between them.

rubric.criterion: Explains po (expression -O --) evaluates expressions to print textual debug descriptions using CustomDebugStringConvertible.
Explains p (expression --) evaluates expressions to print full Swift type information and assigns a temporary $R result variable.
Explains v (frame variable) reads stack memory directly without compilation, making it fast and safe from unintended side effects.

questions.modelAnswer:
In LLDB, po, p, and v serve different variable inspection needs:

1. po (print object) compiles and evaluates an expression, printing the object description string formatted by CustomDebugStringConvertible or debugDescription. It is ideal for human-readable summaries.
2. p (print) compiles an expression and displays the raw data structure with full Swift type information. It also stores the result in a temporary variable like $R0 for subsequent debugger commands.
3. v (frame variable) reads memory directly from debug symbols without compiling an expression context. It executes instantly and cannot trigger side effects, making it the safest tool for reading local variables.

questions.prompt: What are Conditional Breakpoints and Action Breakpoints, and how do they speed up debugging compared to print statements?

rubric.criterion: Explains conditional breakpoints evaluate boolean expressions to pause only on target loop iterations or states without manual clicking.
Explains action breakpoints with automatic continue log live messages without rebuilding or polluting git commits with print statements.

questions.modelAnswer:
Conditional Breakpoints and Action Breakpoints save substantial debugging time compared to print statements:

A Conditional Breakpoint pauses execution only when a boolean condition evaluates to true, like index == 500. This avoids clicking Continue hundreds of times in large loops.

An Action Breakpoint performs tasks when hit, such as logging a message with variable interpolation. By checking 'Automatically continue after evaluating actions', developers can inject live logs into the console without pausing.

Compared to print statements, both breakpoint types eliminate recompilation time on large projects and prevent accidental commits of temporary debugging code.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between Step Over, Step Into, and Step Out during an active debugging session.

rubric.criterion: Explains Step Over (n) executes the current line and pauses at the next line in the same function frame.
Explains Step Into (s) enters the implementation of the function being called on the current line.
Explains Step Out (finish) executes the remainder of the current function and pauses at the return point in the caller.

questions.modelAnswer:
During an active debugging session in Xcode or LLDB:

1. Step Over (n command): Executes the current line of code and pauses at the next line within the same function frame. It does not enter functions called on that line.
2. Step Into (s command): Jumps inside the function being called on the current line, pausing at its first instruction. This lets you inspect inner function logic.
3. Step Out (finish command): Runs the remainder of the current function until it returns, pausing execution immediately in the calling function frame.

questions.prompt: What is an Exception Breakpoint, and why is it one of the first breakpoints every iOS developer should configure?

rubric.criterion: Explains that an Exception Breakpoint catches crashes and exceptions at the exact throw site before the call stack unwinds.
Explains that without it, crashes often highlight AppDelegate or main.swift without showing the originating code line.

questions.modelAnswer:
An Exception Breakpoint instructs Xcode to pause execution immediately when an unhandled exception or runtime error is thrown, before the call stack unwinds.

Without an Exception Breakpoint, unhandled crashes (such as unrecognized selectors, fatal errors, or index out-of-range exceptions) cause the stack to collapse. Xcode then highlights AppDelegate or main.swift with a generic crash message, hiding where the bug occurred.

With an Exception Breakpoint, Xcode freezes at the exact failing line. It displays local variables and the full call stack.

sources.title: Stepping through code and inspecting variables to isolate bugs (Xcode)

questions.prompt: How can evaluating expressions in LLDB cause accidental bugs during a debugging session, and how can you avoid this?

rubric.criterion: Explains that p and po execute code live in process memory, so calling mutating methods alters actual application state.
Explains how to avoid side effects: use v (frame variable) for reading variables directly, or evaluate only pure read-only expressions.

questions.modelAnswer:
Evaluating expressions in LLDB with p or po compiles code dynamically and executes it inside the running application address space.

Evaluating mutating expressions like p counter += 1 permanently alters process memory. Calling methods that update databases also mutates live state. Subsequent logic will run against this altered state, leading to false bugs or unexpected failures.

To avoid accidental state mutation, developers should use v (frame variable) to inspect local memory without expression evaluation. When using p, evaluate only read-only properties and pure getters.
